problem: On a shelf, there are $11$ novels and $9$ science books. $1$ of the novels and $3$ of the science books are illustrated. The illustrated novel is taken from the shelf and set apart. If a single book is selected at random, what is the probability that it is a novel or an illustrated book?

feedback.problem: A number is picked from $10$ to $19.$ What is the probability of picking an even number or a prime number?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $E$ be the event that the picked number is an even number, and let $R$ be the event that the picked number is a prime number. Then the probability that the selected number is an even number or a prime number is $P(E\cup R).$

Given that all prime numbers between $10$ and $19$ are odd, $E$ and $R$ are mutually exclusive events, i.e., $P(E\cap R)=0.$

We can find $P(E)$ and $P(R)$ by computing the necessary ratios. There are $10$ numbers from  $10$ to $19$, of which  $5$ are even, and $4$ are prime.   Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(E) & =\frac{5}{10} \\ P(R) & =\frac{4}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(E\cup R) & =P(E)+P(R)-P(E\cap R) \\  & =\frac{5}{10}+\frac{4}{10}-0 \\  & =\frac{9}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
